proof_summary: For odd primes, Fermat’s theorem makes the powers of 2 periodic modulo \(p\) with exponent period \(p-1\), so shifting indices by \(2(p-1)\) preserves each old summand, including its triangular exponent; every newly introduced summand vanishes because its product contains the factor at index \(p-1\) or \(2(p-1)\). For \(p=2\), all summands except the initial one vanish modulo 2, leaving the constant residue 1.
